transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. To start off, can you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Well, I guess what brings me in is that I just can't seem to keep my mind on one thing anymore. 

I work in a warehouse, and lately, every little noise pulls me off my count. Like, if a beeper goes off, or a forklift alarm, or even just someone moving a pallet across the floor... I completely lose my train of thought. And then I look down and realize I've gone and put the wrong numbers into the inventory. It's getting to be a real problem for my work.
Have you always had trouble staying focused and getting easily distracted, even back in school as a child, or is this a new problem that started recently?

No, it's definitely a new thing. I never really had trouble with it back in school or anything like that. 

It's really just been going on for about a month now. My husband recently stopped working outside the home, and... well, our usual routine completely changed. It seems like ever since then, I just haven't been able to keep my focus.
Since your husband's schedule changed about a month ago, have you noticed yourself feeling unusually worried, anxious, or on edge, separate from the concentration problems?

No, not really. I mean, I'm not any more worried or anxious than usual. It's just the focus thing that's really bothering me. I don't feel on edge or anything like that, just... easily thrown off track at work.
Since your husband's schedule changed, have you noticed yourself feeling down, sad, or overwhelmed by the change, even if you're not anxious?

No, I haven't felt sad or down at all. I mean, it's not a bad thing that he's home now, so I wouldn't say I'm overwhelmed by it either. My mood has been completely fine. It really is just... just this weird inability to focus at the warehouse.
Do you notice this same trouble concentrating happening outside of work too—like at home, while driving, or during conversations—or does it really only happen at the warehouse?

No, it's pretty much everywhere. I mean, it's definitely worse at work because I have to pay attention to what I'm moving, but... yeah, even at home. If my husband is talking to me, I'll just kind of zone out or forget what we were just saying. Or if I'm trying to read something, I just can't stick with it. So it's not just the warehouse, it's kind of all over the place.
When you think about your husband's schedule change, do you feel any inner tension or distress about that adjustment, even if you wouldn't call it worry or sadness?

No, not really. I mean, it's an adjustment having him around during the day now, but it doesn't bother me. There's no tension or anything like that. I'm just having a hard time keeping my mind on things.
How has your sleep been over the past month—are you falling asleep easily, staying asleep, and waking up feeling rested?

My sleep has been pretty normal, honestly. I usually fall asleep without much trouble, and... yeah, I stay asleep through the night. I wake up feeling rested enough for my shift. So, no, I haven't noticed any issues with my sleep at all.
Have you started or changed any medications, supplements, alcohol use, or your caffeine intake around the same time your concentration problems began?

No, nothing like that. I haven't started any new medications or, you know, vitamins or supplements. I don't really drink alcohol, and my coffee routine is exactly the same as it's always been. So... no, no changes there at all.
